requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume on node1 (LUKS-based) mounted at /srv/secure
requirements.summary: A LUKS2 volume (aes-xts-plain64, 512-bit key) was created on a file-backed device /root/secure.img, opened as /dev/mapper/secure, formatted XFS, and mounted at /srv/secure (2.0G, 4% used). Directly observed via cryptsetup luksFormat/luksDump output and df -h/lsblk showing the mount.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot, with no manual/interactive steps
requirements.summary: Healthy pre-reboot baseline was captured (test file written/read, mount active, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service active, boot_id 03408ac4...). A real reboot was issued and acknowledged (connection dropped, exec unreachable for ~9s), and post-reboot the boot_id changed to 2d2a8e51..., confirming an actual restart. After the restart, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service was active with journal entries showing automatic attach using the keyfile (no prompt), /srv/secure was mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and the pre-reboot test file content was intact -- demonstrating the full baseline-disruption-recovery transition required for boot-time automation claims. The crypttab entry uses a root-only (mode 400) keyfile so no interactive passphrase is needed, and both crypttab/fstab use nofail so boot is not blocked on failure.

overall_summary: The task's two material outcomes -- an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure, and automatic unlock/mount at boot -- are both directly and coherently satisfied. The executor performed a genuine reboot (boot_id changed from 03408ac4... to 2d2a8e51...) and captured a full healthy-baseline / disruption / recovery cycle showing the LUKS volume auto-unlocked via keyfile and the filesystem remounted with data intact, with no interactive input. Operational hygiene is good overall; the only issue is a minor leftover /tmp/reboot.log artifact.
limitations: Evidence for auto-unlock relies on a single reboot cycle; repeated reboot resilience was not tested, though this is not required by the task wording.

The keyfile is stored unencrypted on the same root filesystem as the OS, a standard but noteworthy trust-boundary limitation for data-at-rest confidentiality against an attacker with root/disk access; not a violation of the stated task (auto-unlock at boot was the requirement).
Node1 was the only managed node in this topology, so the provider-wide restart evidence protocol is satisfied by the single reboot performed; no cross-node evidence gaps exist.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command history reviewed chronologically: cmd-c83d66352636431e and cmd-bd914ad3eaf64542 are read-only diagnostics with no mutation. cmd-7f248f473981415b (attempted openssl rand keyfile) failed before any file was created (chmod/chown/ls on the nonexistent file also failed, confirming no residue) and was immediately corrected by cmd-480adccaee0f4582 using dd -- a legitimate corrective retry, not an unnecessary mutation. cmd-573dbd6a28b441a2 (umount/luksClose/add crypttab entry/start service) is a bounded, purposeful step to validate and finalize the crypttab-based unlock before adding the fstab entry, not a throwaway experiment. One minor residue: the reboot-issuing command (cmd-514367fa95ed4d0c) left a stray /tmp/reboot.log file on the node (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot), a low-risk artifact of the nohup redirection that was not cleaned up.
